title: The Two Sharpers Who Tricked Each Other

keywords: tale of the two sharpers who each cozened his compeer
full_text:
Two celebrated confidence tricksters—one from Cairo and the other from Damascus—met by chance at a roadside caravanserai near the Dead Sea. Each perceived that his companion was a master of the trade, and each resolved to swindle the other before sunset.

The Cairene sharper displayed a heavy leather bag filled with copper slugs coated in gold leaf, offering to sell it as a purse of pure dinars at a discount.

The Syrian sharper displayed an exquisite silk pouch supposedly filled with rare musk and ambergris, which was actually common clay perfumed with a drop of rosewater.

After an elaborate negotiation of solemn oaths, complimentary flattery, and mutual embraces, the trade was completed: the Cairene took the 'musk,' and the Syrian took the 'gold,' and both parted with immense secret satisfaction, each gloating over his victory.

At the next oasis, the Cairene opened his pouch and smelled common clay! At that exact same moment, the Syrian opened his bag and scratched the copper slugs!

Both burst into roaring laughter across the desert.

They turned their mules around, met again at the caravanserai, embraced with genuine professional admiration, and swore an oath of honest partnership: 'If we can deceive each other with such peerless art, let us abandon swindling and establish an honest import guild!' They became prosperous legitimate merchants, having met their match in wit.
moral: When two cunning tricksters meet, their mutual deception ends in a fair draw and an alliance of wit.
